Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

candidates.cover_letter:
April L. Rorabaugh, Ed.D., LCMHC
Statesville, North Carolina
rorabaughapril@gmail.com
813-842-6018

October 14, 2026


Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to express my interest in the Clinic Director position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor with an Ed.D. in Community Care and Counseling: Traumatology and more than 15 years of experience in behavioral health, clinical services, and program leadership, I bring a strong commitment to providing high-quality, trauma-informed care to adolescents and families.

Throughout my career, I have worked extensively with youth experiencing complex behavioral health challenges, trauma histories, family instability, and barriers to accessing appropriate treatment. In my leadership role with Partners Health Management, I have overseen behavioral health initiatives across a 15-county service area, supervised multidisciplinary teams, and helped develop and implement specialized programs designed to improve access to services, strengthen care coordination, and reduce unnecessary higher levels of care.  One of my greatest professional strengths is combining clinical expertise with operational leadership. I have experience supporting clinical decision-making, establishing effective workflows, monitoring quality and compliance, mentoring staff, and collaborating with families, community providers, hospitals, and child welfare agencies. I understand the importance of developing a clinical environment where staff feel supported, families feel heard, and adolescents receive individualized, evidence-based treatment.

My doctoral research focused on the experiences of social workers placing youth in residential treatment within North Carolina's child welfare system. This work further strengthened my understanding of the challenges adolescents and families face when appropriate community-based behavioral health services are unavailable. I am particularly passionate about developing programs that intervene earlier, promote stability, and help youth receive effective treatment in the least restrictive appropriate setting.

The opportunity to contribute to the development and leadership of Adolescent Wellness Academy's North Carolina program is especially appealing. I would welcome the opportunity to help establish a strong clinical culture, support staff development, build community partnerships, and ensure that adolescents and families receive compassionate, effective, and accountable care.  Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, leadership background, and commitment to adolescent mental health could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's success.

Sincerely,
April L. Rorabaugh, Ed.D., LCMHC

Some may experience uncertainty, fear, or frustration. I would aim to make their first interaction with the organization reassuring and informative, while remaining mindful of professional boundaries, program eligibility, and the importance of connecting individuals with appropriate resources.

As a future social work professional, I value empathy, advocacy, ethical practice, and meeting people where they are. I would welcome the opportunity to apply these values in a role that helps adolescents and families access the care they need. I am eager to contribute to a team that recognizes the importance of making behavioral health services more approachable and ensuring families feel supported from their very first interaction.

Sincerely,

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Operations Manager – Adolescent Behavioral Health position. With over 20 years of experience in behavioral health, clinical services, program development, and organizational leadership, I bring a combination of clinical expertise and operational management experience that aligns well with the demands of overseeing behavioral health programs serving adolescents and their families.

Throughout my career, I have developed a strong foundation in program operations, staff supervision, quality improvement, regulatory compliance, and multidisciplinary collaboration. As the founder and Clinical Director of a behavioral health practice, I have directed clinical and administrative operations, developed policies and procedures, managed budgets and performance oversight, and led a multidisciplinary team of seven therapists and two administrative staff. My responsibilities have required balancing clinical quality, operational efficiency, ethical standards, and organizational growth while maintaining a strong commitment to individualized, trauma-informed care.

My experience also includes direct work with youth and vulnerable populations. As a Program Coordinator with Teen Living Programs, I supported children, youth, and young adults experiencing housing instability, coordinated community partnerships, supervised staff and interns, and contributed to program development and resource allocation. These responsibilities strengthened my understanding of the importance of structured, responsive programming, coordinated services, and organizational accountability when supporting young people navigating complex psychosocial challenges.

In addition, my clinical background includes working with individuals experiencing severe and persistent mental illness, trauma, substance use concerns, and other complex behavioral health needs. Through my work in Assertive Community Treatment and other clinical settings, I have developed expertise in crisis intervention, risk management, interdisciplinary coordination, and evidence-based treatment planning. I understand the importance of effective clinical oversight, clear operational protocols, staff development, and collaboration among providers to promote safety, continuity of care, and positive outcomes.

I would bring to this role a leadership approach that integrates clinical integrity with strategic and operational thinking. My strengths include developing effective programs, supporting and holding teams accountable, improving workflows, fostering collaborative partnerships, and ensuring that services remain responsive to the needs of the populations they serve. I am particularly interested in opportunities where I can apply my behavioral health leadership experience to strengthen adolescent services, support multidisciplinary teams, and contribute to programs that promote stability, resilience, and long-term well-being.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, program leadership, and operational experience could contribute to the continued success of your adolescent behavioral health services.

Sincerely,  
Romel Santiago, MSW, LCSW

candidates.summary:
As a Behavioral Technician, I provide daily support and supervision to adolescents in recovery who experience behavioral challenges and require structured treatment and guidance. My responsibilities include monitoring behaviors, observing changes in mood and behavior, documenting daily observations and client progress, maintaining a safe and supportive environment, reinforcing appropriate coping skills, and assisting with treatment plan implementation. I collaborate with the treatment team to communicate concerns, support individualized treatment goals, and promote continuity of care. This role requires patience, strong documentation skills, confidentiality, attention to detail, and the ability to respond appropriately to challenging situations.

In my previous role as an assistant for a therapy company, I gained experience working with insurance agencies and handling insurance-related administrative responsibilities. My experience included communicating with insurance representatives regarding coverage and benefits, assisting with insurance claims, gathering and verifying patient and policy information, following up on claim statuses, helping resolve billing or claim discrepancies, and maintaining accurate documentation. I also developed an understanding of the importance of insurance eligibility, coverage requirements, timely submissions, and coordination between healthcare providers and insurance payers to help prevent interruptions in treatment.

Together, these experiences have strengthened my knowledge of behavioral health services, insurance coordination, patient documentation, case tracking, and administrative support. I am comfortable managing sensitive information, communicating professionally with multiple parties, and staying organized while handling time-sensitive responsibilities. I am eager to apply these transferable skills to utilization review, insurance authorization coordination, and supporting access to medically necessary behavioral health treatment.

Dear Hiring Committee, 

Thank you for taking the time to review my resume and cover letter. I am writing to express my enthusiasm for the opportunity to continue my experience working as a Registered Mental Health Counseling Intern at  Adolescent Wellness Academy. Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a doctoral candidate in Clinical Psychology with experience in psychotherapy, psychological assessment, crisis intervention, and trauma-informed care, I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your team.

Throughout my career, I have worked with children, adolescents, adults, and families navigating complex emotional and behavioral challenges. My experience includes individual, group, and family therapy, clinical assessments, treatment planning, and interdisciplinary collaboration. I approach my work with empathy, clinical integrity, and a genuine commitment to helping individuals recognize their strengths and achieve meaningful growth.

I am particularly passionate about supporting adolescents during such a pivotal stage of development and believe that a compassionate, collaborative therapeutic relationship can make a lasting difference in their lives.

Thank you for considering my application. I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to the meaningful work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Warm regards,
Claudette Donnarumma

candidates.summary: My professional experience encompasses clinical psychology, mental health counseling, neuropsychological assessment, substance use treatment, crisis intervention, and child and adult protective services. I have worked with diverse populations, including children, adolescents, adults, and families, across outpatient, residential, community-based, and multidisciplinary settings. My clinical responsibilities have included individual, group, and family therapy; psychological and biopsychosocial assessments; diagnostic formulation; individualized treatment planning; suicide risk assessment; and evidence-based interventions for trauma, substance use disorders, and co-occurring psychiatric conditions. Additionally, my experience in child advocacy and protective services has strengthened my expertise in crisis management, interdisciplinary collaboration, legal proceedings, and advocacy for vulnerable populations. As a doctoral candidate in Clinical Psychology, I continue to integrate clinical practice, psychological assessment, research, and leadership to advance culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and person-centered care.

work_history.title: Substance Abuse Therapist
work_history.company_name: Harbor Village Detox and Residential Center
work_history.summary: Conducted individual and group therapy sessions for patients with substance use disorders at ASAM Levels 2.5 and 3.5, utilizing evidence-based interventions. Educated patients on the disease model of addiction, triggers, relapse processes, the role of MAT in recovery, and long-term recovery planning. Facilitated psychoeducational and process groups focused on relapse prevention, emotional regulation, coping skills, and recovery-oriented behavior change. Completed comprehensive biopsychosocial assessments (BPS), integrated clinical summaries, and ASAM dimensional evaluations to determine appropriate level of care and treatment planning. Developed and implemented individualized treatment plans (MTPs) with measurable goals and objectives, regularly updating based on patient progress and clinical presentation. Provided crisis intervention and risk assessment, including suicide risk screenings and safety planning when clinically indicated. Maintained accurate and timely clinical documentation in compliance with regulatory standards, including SOAP notes, treatment plan reviews, and discharge summaries. Utilized evidence-based modalities such as Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Motivational Interviewing (MI), and trauma-informed approaches to support recovery. Collaborated with multidisciplinary team members, including medical providers, nursing staff, case managers, and behavioral health technicians, to coordinate patient care. Monitored patient engagement, treatment adherence, and behavioral patterns, addressing barriers to recovery such as ambivalence, anxiety, and co-occurring mental health symptoms. Educated patients on the disease model of addiction, triggers, relapse processes, and long-term recovery planning. Demonstrated cultural competence and sensitivity when working with diverse patient populations with complex psychosocial needs.

work_history.title: Substance Abuse Therapist
work_history.summary: Conducted therapeutic sessions for individuals and groups, addressing a range of mental health challenges, including substance use disorders, trauma, depression, anxiety, and co-occurring disorders. 6 Collaborated with clients to create personalized, strengths-based treatment plans, setting realistic goals and tracking progress to encourage recovery and long-term wellness. Utilized evidence-based assessment tools to evaluate clients' mental health and substance use issues, providing accurate diagnoses and tailoring interventions accordingly. Responded to crises with appropriate interventions, ensuring the safety of clients and providing immediate support as needed. Worked closely with psychiatrists, social workers, case managers, and other healthcare professionals to provide integrated care and support comprehensive treatment strategies. Maintained detailed and confidential records of client sessions, progress notes, and treatment adjustments, in compliance with organizational and regulatory standards. Led educational sessions to empower clients with knowledge about mental health, coping strategies, relapse prevention, and life skills for enhanced resilience and independence. Assisted clients in navigating community resources, advocating for additional services, and supporting access to housing, employment, and healthcare as part of a holistic recovery process.

October 25, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator: Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With an MBA and a professional background spanning behavioral healthcare operations, substance use treatment, client services, and program administration, I bring a strong combination of leadership, communication, and organizational skills that align with the needs of your admissions team.

Most recently, I served as Director of Operations at Zephyr Behavioral Health & Wellness, where I was responsible for supporting daily operations, regulatory compliance, staff coordination, clinical documentation processes, and organizational readiness. This experience strengthened my understanding of behavioral healthcare delivery, patient confidentiality, HIPAA requirements, and the importance of maintaining efficient systems that support both clinical teams and the individuals seeking treatment.

In addition to my operational leadership experience, I have worked directly within substance use recovery environments, facilitating behavioral health and wellness groups focused on relapse prevention, healthy routines, coping strategies, and long-term recovery. These experiences have reinforced my ability to communicate with individuals facing difficult circumstances while maintaining professionalism, empathy, and a supportive approach.

What particularly interests me about Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to providing compassionate, individualized treatment while supporting families throughout the recovery process. I understand that the admissions experience is often the first meaningful interaction an individual or family has with a treatment provider. Establishing trust, clearly explaining treatment options, coordinating next steps, and maintaining consistent communication can make a significant difference in helping someone access the care they need.

My background has also equipped me with strong administrative, documentation, and follow-through skills, along with experience navigating behavioral healthcare systems and collaborating with multidisciplinary teams. I am comfortable managing competing priorities, maintaining confidentiality, and ensuring that important details are addressed accurately and promptly.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience and dedication to both Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I am confident that my combination of behavioral healthcare leadership, direct recovery support experience, and commitment to exceptional client service would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience align with your organization's mission and goals.

Sincerely,
Jay Miller, MBA

Madison Mrakitsch Lansing, MI

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Bachelor of Science in Psychology with a concentration in Mental Health from Central Michigan University, graduating magna cum laude, and hands-on experience supporting children with autism and other cognitive disabilities as a Registered Behavior Technician at Acorn Health, I have developed a strong foundation in behavioral health, compassionate communication, and individualized care. I am eager to apply my background to help individuals and families navigate the admissions process and connect with the treatment and support they need.

In my role as a Registered Behavior Technician, I work one-on-one with children with autism and other developmental needs in clinical and in-home settings. I implement individualized treatment plans, collect and analyze behavioral data, document client progress, and collaborate with Board Certified Behavior Analysts and interdisciplinary teams. This experience has strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy, maintain accurate documentation, follow established procedures, and recognize the importance of individualized, evidence-based care. It has also given me a deeper appreciation for the challenges families may face when seeking behavioral health services and the importance of making their first interactions with a treatment provider welcoming, informative, and supportive.

My background in customer service and hospitality has further developed my interpersonal communication, organization, and follow-through. Through my work at Good Sense Coffee and Chemung Hills Golf Club, I gained experience assisting diverse customers, managing competing priorities, handling financial transactions accurately, and maintaining a professional, positive demeanor in fast-paced environments. These skills would translate well to responding to admissions inquiries, coordinating assessments and intake appointments, communicating next steps clearly, and following up consistently with prospective clients and referral sources.

Additionally, my academic training in psychology and mental health has provided me with a strong understanding of behavioral health needs and the importance of connecting individuals with appropriate resources. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming experience for both individuals and their loved ones. I would approach every interaction with patience, respect, and compassion while helping callers understand available treatment options and navigate the admissions process. I also recognize the importance of confidentiality, accurate recordkeeping, and clear communication when handling sensitive client information.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it combines my educational background in psychology, my direct experience in behavioral health, and my passion for helping individuals access meaningful support. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to both Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center by helping create a smooth, supportive, and organized experience for clients and families from their first inquiry through admission.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, communication skills, and commitment to compassionate client care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Sincerely, Madison Mrakitsch

Shakora Pounds

4312 Creekdale Dr
Greensboro, NC, 27406

October 25, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy / Principles Recovery Center

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With experience in behavioral healthcare, patient services, administrative operations, and healthcare systems, I am eager to contribute my skills to an organization committed to helping individuals and families access the mental health and substance use treatment they need.

During my time at Crossroads Treatment Center, I gained valuable experience in a substance use treatment setting, supporting patients and assisting with daily administrative operations. This experience strengthened my understanding of the importance of compassionate communication, confidentiality, accurate documentation, and treating every patient with dignity and respect. I recognize that reaching out for treatment can be an overwhelming experience for individuals and families, and I would approach each interaction with patience, empathy, and professionalism.

I also have experience working remotely during staffing shortages, inclement weather, and periods of illness. Although my remote work was not full-time, these opportunities allowed me to become comfortable completing responsibilities outside the traditional office environment. I am confident in my ability to adapt to remote or hybrid work, remain organized, communicate effectively, and manage assigned responsibilities independently.

Additionally, I have experience with healthcare systems and resources, including Availity, athenahealth, and the Virginia Department of Medical Assistance Services (DMAS). My familiarity with these platforms, combined with my education in Medical Billing and Coding, has strengthened my understanding of healthcare administration, medical documentation, and insurance-related processes. I understand the importance of accuracy, timely follow-up, and protecting sensitive patient information in accordance with HIPAA requirements.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to combine my healthcare experience with meaningful patient support. I would welcome the opportunity to assist prospective patients and families with inquiries, explain the admissions process, coordinate assessments and intake appointments, support insurance verification, and maintain accurate records throughout the admissions process. I am committed to helping each caller feel heard, supported, and informed about the next steps toward receiving care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral healthcare background, familiarity with healthcare systems, and commitment to patient-centered service would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Sincerely,
Shakora Pounds

I would like to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Counselor position. 

 

I have clerical experience working at a veterans housing facility for several years and through my work as a supply administrative clerk in the USMC. My paraprofessional work experience included clerical responsibilities also. In addition, I have gained customer service skills by working in retail for a few companies. 

Originally, when I started working in the education field, I started as a paraprofessional working on call and had a few permanent positions at many locations with both the San Jose Unified School District and Santa Clara County Office of Education with mostly Moderate to Severe students. I do, however, have experience with Mild to Moderate also. I have learned such things as busing, feeding, hand-over-hand, one-on-one, and small group instruction, which included adaptation to the expectations of student performance. Through several decades, I have worked in Special Education, moving up my professional position from paraprofessional, temporary campus supervisor, and Kindergarten teaching aide in Merced, CA. I have also been a job coach and childcare worker at residential treatment facilities with both teenage boys and teenage girls, which also included an adult residential house for those with challenges. Though the latter is a substitute position, I have worked 3 years in a long-term substitute position. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am a highly motivated medical assistant with a strong work ethic, a passion for helping others, and a commitment to providing exceptional patient care. With four years of customer service experience, extensive education in the medical assisting field, and a willingness to continually learn and grow, I bring a combination of clinical knowledge, compassion, and professionalism to the healthcare environment.

Throughout my experience in customer service and childcare, I have developed strong communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm and effective in high-pressure situations. I understand the importance of making every patient feel valued, respected, and comfortable. I believe exceptional healthcare extends beyond clinical skills; it also requires empathy, reliability, and a genuine commitment to meeting each patient’s needs.

For the past six years, I have dedicated myself to being a full-time mother to my four children. Although I have been out of the traditional workforce during this time, motherhood has further strengthened my ability to multitask, prioritize responsibilities, solve problems, adapt to changing situations, and manage competing demands with patience and efficiency. These are skills I believe translate directly into a busy medical practice, where organization, teamwork, and attention to detail are essential. I am excited to return to the workforce and apply both my previous professional experience and the skills I have continued to develop during this chapter of my life.

My education at an accredited medical assisting program provided me with a strong foundation in clinical procedures, including obtaining accurate vital signs, performing venipuncture, conducting basic laboratory testing, and collecting thorough and accurate patient histories and subjective assessments. I completed approximately 1,000 hours of clinical laboratory training, in addition to comprehensive classroom instruction, which gave me valuable hands-on experience and a solid understanding of the responsibilities of a medical assistant.

My previous childcare experience also taught me the importance of vigilance, sound judgment, and maintaining a safe environment, particularly when working in situations where even the smallest detail matters. Combined with my patient-focused mindset and dedication to providing quality service, these experiences have prepared me to contribute positively to a healthcare team.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my compassion, strong work ethic, clinical training, and eagerness to learn to your medical practice. I am committed to refreshing my skills, adapting to current office procedures, and becoming a dependable member of your team while helping ensure patients receive the highest standard of care.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and dedication could benefit your clinic. I look forward to hearing from you.

Respectfully, 
Megan Holsonback

Dear Hiring Manager, 

I am currently seeking to showcase and enhance my social services, case management, and human development skills.

I am a dedicated social services professional with 10+ years of experience supporting vulnerable populations through crisis intervention, case management, client screening, referrals, and care coordination. I am experienced in behavioral health, substance abuse, trauma-informed care, documentation, and client communication, with a Master’s degree in Social Work
in progress. I am a skilled at guiding clients toward appropriate resources and maintaining accurate records.



In my current role as a Financial Support Worker I Manage multiple client cases independently, maintaining accurate documentation and consistent follow-up and provide clear understanding of next steps in the process. A previous role as a Medicaid Case Manager I provided resources for clients by working with various agencies and providers in the community to ensure each client was able to remain safely living in their home,  thus preventing long term care facility placement.



In a former role as an ADA Specialist, I was the liaison for the employer and the employee. I ensured both were successful by providing complete support from beginning to end of each individual case. This included data entry, claim and file management, requesting and compiling medical documents, evaluating those documents to determine if an employee’s medical condition is substantially limiting under the Americans with Disability Act, and compiling a summary to the employer for further review. 


As a Resident Assistant I supervised and managed up to 18 women who were in recovery and struggled with mental health wellbeing. They were all from different backgrounds and lifestyles. I provided emotional and mental support by ensuring each woman knew her importance in this world and that they have a purpose. I encouraged them to maintain their treatment plans and provided necessary skills to cope with life outside of addiction. Working in a recovery atmosphere, no day is ever the same. This has helped me adapt in any atmosphere and situation. 

I believe I will be a great asset to your company and hope to be considered to partner with you in the near future.

Thanks,

Deborrah Latham Whiteside

Re: Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Admissions Coordinator position with your organization. With over five years of experience in behavioral health admissions and a broader background in mental health, substance use disorder treatment, and crisis support, I bring a strong understanding of the admissions process and the importance of connecting individuals with the appropriate level of care.

Throughout my career, I have worked directly with individuals and families seeking treatment during some of the most challenging moments of their lives. My experience includes handling incoming admissions inquiries, conducting initial screenings, gathering relevant information, verifying insurance benefits, coordinating with clinical and admissions teams, and helping prospective clients navigate the process of entering treatment. I understand the importance of responding promptly, communicating compassionately, maintaining confidentiality, and balancing the needs of prospective patients with the operational requirements of a treatment program.

I recognize that the admissions process is often a critical first step toward recovery. I strive to make every interaction professional, supportive, and informative while helping individuals and families feel heard and understood. I am comfortable managing competing priorities, handling sensitive conversations, and working in fast-paced environments where attention to detail, sound judgment, and follow-through are essential.

I am particularly interested in a remote opportunity where I can apply my behavioral health experience, strong communication skills, and commitment to helping people access treatment. I am dependable, adaptable, and comfortable working independently while collaborating with a team to meet organizational goals and provide a positive experience for those seeking care.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and dedication to behavioral health admissions could contribute to your organization and the individuals you serve.

Sincerely,
Holly Brim

I am particularly interested in bringing these skills to an admissions role serving adolescents and their families. I am dependable, adaptable, detail-oriented, and comfortable working in high-demand environments where professionalism and compassion are essential.

Thank you for considering my application. Sincerely,
Jasmine Kirby

candidates.summary:
My experience in healthcare has given me a unique perspective from both sides of care - providing direct, hands-on support as a Patient Care Provider and guiding families through their most vulnerable moments as a Virtual Health Provider. As a Patient Care Provider, I learned that care is more than tasks. It is about presence. I supported patients with activities of daily living, safety monitoring, vital signs, and objective documentation, while working with individuals experiencing anxiety, depression, mood disorders, psychosis, and substance use challenges. This role taught me how to stay calm in crisis, use therapeutic communication and de-escalation, recognize subtle changes in behavior, and always maintain dignity, boundaries, and HIPAA compliance. I learned to listen without judgment and to report early, because in behavioral health, early observation saves lives. 
Transitioning to a Virtual care provider deepened that understanding. In this role, I was often the first point of contact for parents and guardians who were scared, overwhelmed, and seeking immediate help for their child. Virtually, I conducted compassionate intake screenings, gathered psychosocial history, assessed for safety risks including self-harm and suicidal ideation, verified benefits, and coordinated with clinical, nursing, and utilization review teams to ensure appropriate and timely admissions. Working specifically with the adolescent population taught me how to balance empathy with professionalism. I had to speak calmly to a teen in distress one moment, and then provide clear, reassuring education to their family the next. I became skilled at crisis triage, active listening, de-escalating high-emotion calls, and explaining complex treatment processes in simple, hopeful terms.

LEILA MORDAUNT

107 S Mulberry St, Statesboro, GA 30-458 (562) 242-6534 |

APPLICATION FOR VIRTUAL ADMISSIONS COORDINATOR

October 24, 2026

Hiring Team

Adolescent Wellness Academy & Principles Recovery Center

Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position because I know how much it matters to reach a compassionate, knowledgeable person when a family is trying to find mental-health care. My interest in this work comes not only from professional caregiving but also from years of personally helping someone I love navigate a complicated treatment system.

When my younger sister was 15, I became her guardian and foster caregiver. After about a month, she needed to return to Hawaii because she could not obtain the medical benefits in California that would allow her to continue her psychiatric medication. Although she returned to state care, I remained actively involved in her life and treatment. I researched programs, called facilities, arranged evaluations and appointments, prepared documentation, coordinated with social workers and clinical teams, and transported her between placements and services when she returned to California. I communicated with psychiatrists, therapists, hospitals, residential programs, and case managers, often following up repeatedly to make sure there was a next step rather than another dead end.

Most recently, I helped her connect with an adult program offering housing, work, and educational support. That transition means a great deal to me. It reflects something I learned throughout the process: families and individuals seeking care do not always know what to ask, what they qualify for, or where to turn. Clear explanations, dependable follow-through, and a person who stays engaged can make an enormous difference.

My professional work has reinforced those same values. As a caregiver and special-needs swim instructor, 1 have supported clients with complex daily needs, communicated directly with families, and adapted my approach to each person. I also bring experience answering and screening calls in a receptionist role, managing client schedules independently, and maintaining demanding online college coursework. I am comfortable working independently, learning new systems, and treating sensitive personal circumstances with care.

Although my experience comes through caregiving, family advocacy, reception, and independently.

coordinated client services rather than a conventional admissions title, I have personally performed many of the resource-navigation and follow-up activities at the heart of this work. I would welcome the opportunity to bring that perspective, a calm and respectful phone presence, and a strong commitment to helping people reach appropriate care to your team.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience could support the individuals and families contacting your programs.

Sincerely,

Leila Mordaunt

I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to help individuals and families navigate the first steps toward mental health and substance use treatment with dignity, understanding, and confidence.
As Lab Manager at Principle Labs, I was responsible for clinical patient intake, chart creation, appointment scheduling, insurance verification, and maintaining accurate patient records. Working directly with patients in a clinical setting strengthened my ability to gather sensitive information, identify needs, answer questions, coordinate next steps, and protect confidential health information. This experience gave me a practical understanding of the administrative processes that support effective treatment access, from the initial patient interaction through documentation and coordination with insurance providers.
My experience as Executive and Development Assistant at Domestic Abuse Services, Inc. further developed the interpersonal and assessment skills essential to admissions work. In this role, I worked within the social services field, supporting individuals and families affected by domestic and sexual violence, teen dating violence, and human trafficking. Through my participation in a 24-hour helpline, I conducted intake and risk assessments, assisted with safety planning, and connected individuals experiencing crisis with appropriate agency and community resources. These responsibilities required empathy, sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to communicate calmly and effectively with people facing difficult and often overwhelming circumstances. They also reinforced my commitment to meeting each person where they are, listening without judgment, and helping them identify a safe and appropriate next step.
In addition to my direct client-support experience, my healthcare background includes surgical scheduling, insurance eligibility and benefits support, patient follow-up, and medical documentation. I am comfortable coordinating information among patients, providers, and insurance representatives, maintaining organized records, and managing competing priorities while ensuring accuracy and confidentiality. My experience with electronic medical record systems and administrative technology, combined with my ability to work independently in a remote environment, would allow me to contribute to a responsive, organized, and compassionate admissions process.
I understand that reaching out for treatment can be a difficult and vulnerable step for both individuals and their families. I would welcome the opportunity to be a reassuring first point of contact—someone who listens carefully, explains the process clearly, follows through consistently, and helps each caller move toward the appropriate care or resources. I believe my combination of clinical intake experience, crisis assessment, resource coordination, and patient-centered communication would enable me to make a meaningful contribution to your team and the individuals you serve.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and commitment to compassionate, confidential care can support the admissions teams at Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your mission of helping individuals and families access the support they need.


Sincerely,
Elizabeth Steele

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With over 25 years of experience in healthcare, customer service, and administration, I believe I have the communication skills, compassion, and attention to detail needed to be successful in this role.

During my time at Henry Ford Health, I worked as a Senior IT Operations Specialist in a fast-paced, call center-based environment. My responsibilities required me to manage multiple systems, coordinate communications, handle sensitive information, and assist individuals during stressful and sometimes critical situations. I became very comfortable working with Epic and other healthcare systems while maintaining professionalism, accuracy, and confidentiality.

I also bring years of experience from the Circuit Court, where I worked in both clerical and supervisory positions. That experience strengthened my ability to listen without judgment, handle difficult conversations, manage confidential records, and follow through on important matters. I understand that people reaching out for help may be overwhelmed, frightened, or unsure of where to begin. I believe having someone on the other end of the phone who is patient, understanding, and genuinely willing to help can make a tremendous difference.

What especially interests me about this position is the opportunity to help adolescents and families take that first step toward getting the care they need. Mental health and substance use challenges can affect an entire family, and I would find it incredibly rewarding to be part of an organization helping people navigate those difficult circumstances.

I am organized, dependable, comfortable learning new technology, and confident in my ability to work independently in a remote environment. I take pride in following through, paying attention to the little details, and treating every person with kindness and respect.

I would truly appreciate the opportunity to bring my experience and dedication to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you.

Sincerely,
Mary Allen

Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. Being the first voice someone hears when they reach out for help is a responsibility I would take seriously. I want people to feel heard, respected, and encouraged as they take that next step.

Through my work as a Behavioral Health Technician and Activity Assistant at Creekside Behavioral Health, I support people facing mental health and substance use challenges. My experience supporting patients and leading in-person groups has helped me build trust, listen without judgment, and communicate with compassion during difficult moments. I would bring those same strengths to conversations with callers and their families.

My own recovery has given me a personal understanding of how difficult asking for help can be. It is also a big part of why I am passionate about helping others. I am continuing my education toward a bachelor’s degree in liberal arts with a specialization in psychology, and I am eager to keep growing in behavioral health.

My background has been in direct patient support rather than a dedicated remote admissions role. I recognize there would be new processes to learn, including insurance verification, admissions tracking, and your CRM and EMR systems. I would approach that training with dedication, ask questions, and work to become a dependable member of your team.

While I may not bring every qualification listed, I bring relevant hands-on experience, a strong desire to learn, and a sincere commitment to helping people. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how those strengths could support your admissions team and the people who reach out to your programs.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Jeff Melton

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. Having worked in both adolescent behavioral health and crisis support, I know that reaching out for help can be difficult for individuals and families. I would love to be part of a team that helps make that process a little easier.

At Sandstone Care, I work directly with adolescents facing mental health, substance use, and behavioral challenges. Before that, I worked remotely at Rocky Mountain Crisis Partners, where I answered crisis calls, assessed callers’ needs and safety, and helped connect them with appropriate services. These experiences taught me how to handle difficult conversations, stay calm under pressure, and make sure people feel heard while working to find the support they need.

I also have experience connecting people with community resources through my work at 2-1-1 Big Bend. Across these roles, I’ve developed strong communication and organizational skills, along with an understanding of how important it is to follow through and treat people with compassion. I would be excited to bring that experience to AWA and help teens and families navigate the admissions process.

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you.

Sincerely,
Meagan Sellards

candidates.cover_letter:
When a parent reaches out to the Adolescent Wellness Center, they are often calling on one of the most stressful days of their life. They need an intake voice who balances clinical precision with immense empathy. As an experienced admissions supervisor and intake professional returning to behavioral health, I am writing to express my enthusiastic interest in the Remote Intake Coordinator position. After taking a planned two-year break to focus full-time on my family as a stay-at-home mom, I am eager to re-enter the workforce in a role dedicated to meaningful, life-changing work for youth and their support systems.

My background directly eliminates any technical or operational ramp-up time for your team. Across my career in treatment management, I progressed from an Admissions Coordinator to Admissions Supervisor. I am deeply proficient in industry-standard software, including KIPU and Salesforce. I’m also experience at independently verifying complex insurance eligibility and navigating prior authorizations smoothly from a remote environment.

Beyond clinical administration, my recent background includes high-volume guest relations within the Atlantic City casino and hospitality industry. While separate from healthcare, this fast-paced environment sharpened my transferable skills in high-stakes customer care: rapid problem-solving, meticulous record-keeping, and the ability to masterfully de-escalate high-stress situations with absolute professionalism. Combined with my core training in motivational interviewing, I know how to connect with anxious caregivers, lower barriers to care, and establish immediate trust.

The chance to support your remote intake pipeline allows me to bring my clinical toolkit, data compliance experience, and a mom’s perspective on family advocacy to your mission. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my diverse operational background can support the adolescent families trusting the Adolescent Wellness Center.

Thank you for your time and consideration!

candidates.cover_letter:
I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With my background in behavioral health and person-centered support, I am passionate about helping adolescents overcome challenges, develop healthy coping strategies, and build the skills needed to achieve greater emotional wellness and personal growth.

My experience in behavioral health has taught me the importance of building trusting relationships, listening without judgment, and approaching each individual with patience, empathy, and respect. I understand that adolescents experiencing emotional, behavioral, or mental health challenges benefit from consistency, structure, encouragement, and a supportive environment where they feel safe and valued.

I believe in meeting individuals where they are while encouraging accountability, self-awareness, and positive change. I also value teamwork, effective communication, and collaboration in providing quality, individualized support. My goal is to help young people recognize their strengths, develop resilience, and feel empowered to move toward a healthier future.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, compassion, and commitment to behavioral health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to your team and the well-being of the adolescents you serve.

Sincerely,
Lisa Bittner

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With prior experience working in a treatment facility and hands-on experience using the Kipu system, I bring valuable knowledge of treatment admissions, client communication, and the importance of helping individuals access the care and support they need.

My experience in a treatment environment has given me an understanding of the admissions process and the importance of treating every individual with compassion, professionalism, and respect. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be a difficult and vulnerable step, and I believe that creating a welcoming, supportive, and nonjudgmental experience is essential from the very first point of contact.

My familiarity with the Kipu  system has provided me with experience using treatment-related technology and understanding the importance of accurate documentation, organization, and maintaining confidentiality. I am comfortable communicating with individuals, managing information, and helping ensure that the admissions process runs as smoothly as possible.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and understanding of the treatment industry to your team. I am committed to helping individuals navigate the admissions process and take the next step toward recovery while providing the professionalism and compassionate support they deserve.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience would make me a valuable addition to your organization.

Sincerely,
Amy Knight

candidates.cover_letter:
My academic background in psychology and my professional experience supporting individuals and families have shaped my commitment to helping people access the resources and support they need to thrive. I was particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s philosophy of treating people, not symptoms, and its commitment to creating a safe, supportive, and nonjudgmental environment where adolescents and their families can heal and grow together. I believe that helping someone access care begins with making them feel heard, respected, and supported. I would be excited to contribute to this mission as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator by helping adolescents and families navigate the admissions process with compassion, clarity, and understanding.

I earned my Bachelor of Arts from Widener University, where I studied Psychology and Gender and Women’s Studies and minored in International Relations. My academic background provided me with a foundation in human behavior, interpersonal relationships, and the importance of understanding individuals within their broader social and family contexts. Through my academic and professional experiences, I have developed an appreciation for person-centered approaches that recognize each individual's unique circumstances, strengths, and challenges. I would bring this perspective to interactions with families who may be navigating uncertainty or seeking mental health support for their adolescents.

In my current role as an Employment Specialist at DiscoverAbility, I work directly with individuals to identify opportunities that align with their goals, strengths, and needs. I guide participants through the employment process by assisting with applications, developing resumes and cover letters, identifying appropriate opportunities, and maintaining accurate documentation of their progress. This role has strengthened my ability to build rapport, communicate information clearly, provide individualized guidance, and manage responsibilities with attention to detail. Previously, as an intern with Elwyn’s Early Learning Services, I gained experience supporting young children with developmental delays and disabilities and their families. I contributed to efforts focused on promoting child development, strengthening family capacity, and helping families access the support they needed. These experiences reinforced the importance of patience, empathy, and collaboration when working with individuals and families navigating unfamiliar or challenging circumstances.

My experience with Maryland Hunger Solutions further strengthened my ability to connect individuals with essential resources. Through outreach and advocacy initiatives, I collaborated with community partners and assisted individuals in accessing programs such as SNAP, local food banks, and school meal services. I also helped develop communication materials, including Spanish-language resources, to improve accessibility for Spanish-speaking communities. This experience taught me that connecting people with services requires more than providing information; it requires listening to their concerns, explaining available resources in accessible language, and helping them understand their next steps. As someone fluent in both English and Spanish, I would bring this same commitment to culturally responsive communication when interacting with adolescents, parents, and referral partners.

What stands out to me about Adolescent Wellness Academy is its recognition that supporting adolescents also means supporting their families. Seeking mental health treatment can be an overwhelming process for parents and teens alike, and the first interaction with an admissions team can help establish a sense of trust and reassurance. I would approach these conversations with compassion, professionalism, and respect, recognizing the importance of helping each family feel heard while guiding them toward appropriate next steps. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my communication, organizational, and client-support skills to an admissions process that reflects AWA’s commitment to individualized care, family involvement, and lasting growth.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background in psychology, experience supporting individuals and families, and commitment to accessible, person-centered services could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s mission.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, professional experience in applied behavior analysis (ABA), and a background in remote client outreach and appointment coordination, I bring a unique combination of clinical understanding, interpersonal skills, and organizational abilities to this role.

Throughout my career in behavioral health, I have worked directly with individuals and families navigating challenging circumstances. My experience as a Registered Behavior Technician strengthened my ability to communicate compassionately, build trust, maintain professional boundaries, and approach sensitive situations with patience and understanding. I recognize how important it is for individuals seeking treatment to feel heard, respected, and supported from their very first interaction.

In my current remote position as an Appointment Setter with D1 Training, I manage high-volume outreach, engage prospective clients, coordinate appointments, maintain accurate records, and follow up consistently to ensure a positive client experience. This role has strengthened my ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and guide individuals toward appropriate services while maintaining a warm and professional phone presence.

What particularly draws me to this opportunity is the chance to combine my psychology education with my professional strengths in communication and client coordination. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an incredibly vulnerable experience, especially for adolescents and their families. I would take pride in being a reassuring, knowledgeable first point of contact and helping individuals navigate the admissions process with clarity and dignity.

I am confident that my behavioral health background, remote work experience, attention to detail, and genuine commitment to helping others would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills align with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,
Kaylee Charlet

May 11, 2026
Dear Hiring Committee,
I am writing to express my interest in a teaching position within your school district, specifically in Media Arts, Broadcasting, English, or related subject areas. I recently graduated from Northern Kentucky University with a Bachelor’s degree in Electronic Media and Broadcasting as well as an Associate’s degree in English, and I am looking for an opportunity to bring my creativity, communication skills, and classroom experience into a teaching environment.
During my time at Northern Kentucky University, I worked on multiple collaborative media projects that helped me develop leadership, organization, and communication skills. I directed student film projects, worked on scripts and storyboards, operated cameras, and edited video using Adobe Premiere Pro. These experiences taught me how to work closely with others, adapt under pressure, and help creative ideas come together in a productive and supportive environment.
Outside of media work, my current position at Cultivate BHE has had a major impact on how I approach education and communication. I work one-on-one with autistic children in classroom settings where I help students with academic goals, emotional regulation, communication, and everyday life skills. This experience has strengthened my patience, adaptability, and ability to connect with students with different needs and learning styles. It has also shown me how important encouragement and understanding are in helping students succeed.
One project I am especially proud of is a choose-your-own-adventure story game that I developed alongside a 3D-printed interactive game board. The project was designed to be accessible for visually impaired individuals while still being engaging for all users. Creating this project allowed me to combine storytelling, accessibility, and hands-on learning in a way that reflects the kind of creative and inclusive environment I hope to bring into a classroom.
I want to be the kind of teacher who helps students feel comfortable expressing themselves, thinking creatively, and building confidence in their abilities. I believe my background in media production, storytelling, classroom support, and accessibility-focused projects gives me a strong foundation to connect with students and contribute positively to your school community.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I appreciate the opportunity to apply and would welcome the chance to further discuss my qualifications and interest in the position.
Sincerely,

Blayne Pugh

candidates.cover_letter:
Amber Jones
Atlantic City, New Jersey

October 23, 2026

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Intake Coordinator position with your organization. With a bachelor’s degree in Psychology, experience working as an Intake Counselor at Enlightened Solutions, and a genuine passion for helping individuals access the support they need, I believe I would be a valuable addition to your team.

My background in psychology has given me a strong foundation in understanding human behavior, mental health, and the importance of providing compassionate, nonjudgmental support. During my experience as an Intake Counselor, I gained exposure to the intake process within a recovery treatment setting and developed an appreciation for the importance of clear communication, professionalism, and helping individuals navigate the process of seeking care.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it allows me to combine my interest in mental health with my ability to communicate effectively, build rapport, and help individuals take meaningful steps toward treatment. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use support can be difficult, and I believe every caller deserves to feel heard, respected, and supported. I would approach each interaction with empathy while ensuring that inquiries are handled efficiently and that prospective clients receive clear guidance regarding treatment options and next steps.

I am also prepared to contribute to the administrative responsibilities of this role, including coordinating assessments and intake appointments, assisting with documentation, following up with prospective clients, and maintaining accurate records. I understand the importance of confidentiality, attention to detail, consistent follow-through, and accurate documentation when working with sensitive client information. I am eager to continue developing my skills in electronic record systems, customer relationship management platforms, and performance tracking to support both client care and organizational goals.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my psychology background, dedication to helping others, and commitment to compassionate service to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, skills, and passion for mental health can contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,
Amber Jones

To whom it may concern,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With several years of experience working in behavioral health and supportive care settings, along with my ongoing education in psychology, I believe my background and passion for helping others would make me a valuable addition to your team.

From 2021 to 2024, I worked at Ranch Hope, a behavioral school and residential program for adolescent boys. During my time there, I gained hands-on experience supporting adolescents with behavioral and emotional challenges, communicating with parents, completing paperwork, and maintaining accurate documentation. This experience taught me the importance of patience, compassion, confidentiality, and clear communication, especially when working with families navigating difficult situations.

I currently work as a Direct Support Professional at Elwyn, where I continue to support individuals with various needs while maintaining documentation and providing individualized care. I am also pursuing my bachelor’s degree in Psychology at Wilmington University, with a concentration in Mental Health and Wellness.

What interests me most about this opportunity is being able to make a difference from the very first conversation. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be overwhelming, and I would take pride in helping individuals and families feel heard, understood, and comfortable taking that next step.

Although my previous positions have primarily been in person, I have experience independently managing work-related responsibilities outside of my regular work environment. I am organized, dependable, adaptable, and confident in my ability to learn new systems and succeed in a remote position.

I would appreciate the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and genuine passion for mental health to your organization. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of joining your team.

Sincerely,
McKaylee Rossetti
