candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for a position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. When I learned about your work supporting adolescents and their families through mental health treatment, I immediately felt that this was an organization where my education, professional experience, and personal passion for helping others could come together in a meaningful way.

I hold a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from Southern New Hampshire University, graduating with a 3.79 GPA, and I am currently pursuing my master's degree at Grand Canyon University. Continuing my education in this field reflects how seriously I take my goal of building a career centered around mental health and helping others.

My professional background includes more than ten years of experience in behavioral health, customer service, administrative support, and leadership. Earlier in my career, I worked as a Mental Health Technician at Cypress Psychiatric Hospital, where I provided direct support to patients in an inpatient psychiatric setting. I monitored behavior, documented observations for clinical teams, assisted with crisis prevention and de-escalation, and supported patients with daily living and therapeutic activities.

That experience gave me an appreciation for how important it is to have people around you who are willing to listen without judgment and remain calm when someone is struggling. I learned that sometimes the way you communicate with someone can make a difficult situation feel a little less overwhelming. Those are lessons I have carried with me throughout my career.

My more recent experience as a Customer Service Representative and Administrative Assistant has strengthened the organizational and communication skills I would bring to AWA. I have managed high volumes of calls, addressed concerns with empathy and professionalism, coordinated schedules and tasks, maintained accurate documentation, prepared reports, and handled sensitive information while maintaining confidentiality. I am comfortable learning new technology and regularly working with Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams.

I am particularly interested in working with adolescents because I believe early support can make a lasting difference. Teenagers are navigating an incredibly important period of development, and having someone take their concerns seriously can matter more than people sometimes realize. I would approach each interaction with patience, respect, and the understanding that every adolescent and family has a different story and different needs.

I also understand that behavioral health is not only about supporting the individual receiving care. Families often need reassurance, clear communication, organization, and someone who can help them navigate what can be an unfamiliar and stressful process. My combination of behavioral health experience, psychology education, graduate-level study, and administrative and customer-service skills would allow me to support both the human and practical sides of that process.

I would be honored to bring my experience, compassion, reliability, and genuine interest in mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am eager to continue growing within the behavioral health field while pursuing my master's degree, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team dedicated to helping adolescents and families build healthier futures.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to speak with you about how my background and education could contribute to the work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Heather Morris

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With approximately 10 years of experience in the mental health and substance use treatment field, I have developed a strong understanding of the challenges individuals and families face when seeking behavioral health services. I am passionate about helping people access the care they need, and I believe my professional background, personal experiences, and commitment to compassionate, person-centered care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Throughout my career, I have worked with individuals experiencing mental health challenges, substance use disorders, and co-occurring conditions. My experience in behavioral health has strengthened my communication, documentation, coordination, and client advocacy skills. I understand the importance of helping individuals navigate treatment options, communicating clearly with families and providers, and ensuring that people feel supported rather than overwhelmed when taking the first steps toward recovery. I also recognize that timely follow-up, accurate documentation, confidentiality, and organization are essential to helping individuals successfully access appropriate treatment.

In addition to my professional experience, I bring a personal understanding of the impact addiction and mental health challenges can have on individuals and families. I grew up in the foster care system with two parents who struggled with addiction. Those experiences gave me firsthand insight into the instability, uncertainty, and emotional challenges that children and families can experience when substance use affects a household. While my professional experience has provided me with the knowledge and skills to work in behavioral health, my personal experiences have shaped the compassion, empathy, and understanding I bring to every interaction. I recognize that behind every phone call is a person or family who may be experiencing fear, uncertainty, or desperation, and I believe those individuals deserve to be met with dignity, patience, and understanding.

Mikayla Middaugh · Friendship, NY · 607-651-8334 · meekay10@yahoo.com

Dear Hiring Team,
I am writing to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. Most recently I worked overnight in a substance use treatment program, and for years before that I was a paramedic, so I have spent my career being the steady voice for people on some of their hardest days. I would be honored to bring that to families and clients making their first call for help.
As an Overnight Clinical Technician at CASA Trinity, I supported clients in recovery as a 1:1 mentor and documented their progress in the agency's EHR in compliance with NYS OASAS and 42 CFR confidentiality requirements. I coordinated with outside providers and referral sources, handled screening and transportation logistics, and joined weekly interdisciplinary case meetings. That work gave me hands-on experience with the intake-to-treatment pathway your coordinators guide families through, and with protecting the privacy of people seeking care.
My eight years as a paramedic and EMT Crew Chief taught me to build rapport quickly with frightened patients and families, explain what is happening in plain language, and give clear handoffs to physicians and nurses. Today, as a NYS Long Term Care Ombudsman, I investigate complaints, mediate among residents, families, and staff, and track every case through to resolution in organized records. I have also volunteered for years as a crisis advocate and as a moderator in mental health support communities, where I de-escalate people in distress and connect them with appropriate resources.
I know this role demands consistent follow-up and the discipline to manage your own pipeline. My current work is self-directed: I carry my own caseload, set my own priorities, and follow each case until it is resolved. I am comfortable with CRM and EHR documentation and learn new systems quickly, and I am eager to build further skills in Kipu and insurance verification.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to talk about how my experience can help your teams meet every caller with compassion and follow through until each one has a path forward.
Sincerely,
Mikayla Middaugh

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With my background in healthcare administration, medical and dental front desk operations, insurance coordination, and patient support, I have developed the communication, organization, and follow-through skills needed to help individuals navigate the process of accessing care.

Throughout my experience, I have worked directly with patients to coordinate appointments, complete check-in and check-out procedures, review treatment plans, and explain insurance benefits, including copayments, deductibles, annual maximums, and out-of-pocket expenses. I understand that navigating healthcare coverage can be overwhelming, and I take pride in breaking down complex information into clear, understandable terms so patients can make informed decisions about their care.

I have also worked with out-of-network providers to facilitate contracting with insurance networks, helping practices expand their participation in insurance plans. Additionally, I have assisted patients in identifying coverage options that better meet their healthcare needs and financial circumstances. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to manage detailed information, coordinate multiple steps in a process, communicate with different parties, and ensure that important follow-up tasks are not overlooked.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to apply my healthcare administrative experience in a setting where the first interaction can make a meaningful difference in someone’s life. I recognize the importance of approaching sensitive conversations with patience, empathy, professionalism, and respect. Whether speaking with a patient, a family member, or a referring provider, I would strive to make each interaction welcoming while ensuring that inquiries are handled accurately and the appropriate next steps are clearly communicated.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my patient-centered approach, insurance knowledge, attention to detail, and commitment to dependable service to your admissions team. I am eager to contribute to a process that helps individuals and families navigate their options and take the next step toward receiving the care they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Dymond Weathers

They wouldn’t let me start my community service until I was 6 weeks postpartum (& I also had my tubes tied). I had my 1st son at 32 weeks so to be safe we waited. After I started my community service at Goodwill. I ended up being 3 hrs short on community service when I had to go back to court where usually an extension is given & over the years being in a small town or when I was in court for traffic tickets I would see ppl who had never even started community service get an extension multiple times. I was one of the last ppl to see the judge & he wanted to know why it had been a year & my community service wasn’t completed so he asked my lawyer (who was the best in our little town & my parent paid a lot of money too) what he could say for me. Well he said I was a good person who came from a good family instead of explaining I wasn’t allowed to do community service for the 37 weeks plus 6 weeks postpartum. The judge was never told that & so he didn’t give me a 1st time extension to finish so the charge wasn’t dropped & here we are 12 yrs later.

Colorado Springs, CO 80925 ♦ brianna.l.gabbard@gmail.com 

October 22, 2026

RE: Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager: I am writing to express my interest in the position of Virtual Admissions Coordinator for Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment. I am currently pursuing a Master of Arts in Counseling and Human Services with a concentration in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and I am eager to build upon my professional experience while developing my skills as a counselor in a clinical setting.

For nearly a decade, I have worked in secondary education with students and families from a wide range of backgrounds and circumstances. Throughout my career, I have had the opportunity to work alongside individuals from low-socioeconomic and historically disenfranchised populations, as well as individuals whose lives have been impacted by addiction, legal involvement, housing instability, and homelessness. These experiences have shaped the way I understand people and the circumstances that influence their lives. More importantly, they have reinforced my belief that every person deserves to be heard, treated with dignity, and supported without judgment.

My experience in education has taught me that meaningful change often begins with a trusting relationship. As an educator, I have learned to listen carefully, recognize when someone may be struggling beneath the surface, meet individuals where they are, and provide support while respecting their autonomy. I have also seen how trauma, substance use, socioeconomic barriers, family circumstances, and other challenges can affect a person's ability to succeed. These experiences have been an important part of my decision to pursue clinical mental health counseling and licensed addiction counseling.

As a graduate student, I am now seeking an opportunity to translate my academic preparation into meaningful clinical experience. I am most interested in strengthening my counseling skills alongside qualified professionals, developing greater confidence in clinical assessment and treatment, and becoming more intentional in how I support clients through difficult periods of their lives. At this present stage, curiosity, genuineness, and adaptability are the core values that drive my professional attitude. 
I would be grateful for the opportunity to learn and serve at the Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am eager to have the opportunity to grow within your organization while gaining the clinical experience necessary to become a compassionate, ethical, and effective practitioner.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my background, goals, and interest in potentially working with the Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Brianna L. Gabbard

Cover Letter – Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With experience in behavioral health, crisis support, and direct client services, I have developed a strong foundation in compassionate communication, active listening, and helping individuals and families navigate challenging circumstances. I am excited about the opportunity to bring these skills to an organization dedicated to supporting adolescents and their well-being.

My background includes working as a Registered Behavior Technician and providing intensive and respite services, where I support individuals with behavioral and developmental needs. These experiences have strengthened my ability to communicate effectively, remain patient under pressure, maintain professionalism, and approach each individual with empathy and respect. In addition, my work with DeafLEAD in a crisis-support role has reinforced the importance of building trust, responding thoughtfully to sensitive situations, and helping individuals feel heard during vulnerable moments.

I am currently working in a 100% remote position with DeafLEAD, which has provided me with direct experience managing professional responsibilities in a virtual work environment. I have a dedicated, private workspace equipped with the necessary technology, reliable high-speed internet, and the equipment needed to perform my duties effectively. I am confident in my ability to remain productive, communicate professionally, maintain confidentiality, and consistently complete my workload while working remotely. Transitioning into another fully virtual position would be a natural fit for my existing experience and established work environment.

I understand that the admissions process can be an important first step for families seeking behavioral health support for their children. I would approach this responsibility with compassion, organization, and attention to detail, ensuring that prospective families feel welcomed, informed, and supported as they explore available services. I am committed to creating positive first impressions, communicating clearly, and helping families navigate the admissions process with professionalism and sensitivity.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy by combining my behavioral health background, crisis-support experience, and established remote-work capabilities to support both families and the admissions team. I believe my commitment to helping others, adaptability, and ability to work independently would make me a valuable addition to your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Serene Smith

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in behavioral healthcare, a background in pediatric mental health crisis intervention, and a Master’s degree in healthcare administration, I bring a combination of clinical knowledge, communication skills, and administrative understanding that aligns with the needs of this position. I am passionate about helping adolescents and their families navigate the process of accessing appropriate mental health and substance use treatment.

In my current role as a Mental Health Technician at SUN Behavioral Health in Erlanger, Kentucky, I work in a behavioral healthcare environment where patient safety, communication, confidentiality, and collaboration are essential. This experience has strengthened my understanding of behavioral health services and the importance of creating a supportive environment for individuals experiencing emotional and psychological challenges. I have developed the ability to remain professional in stressful situations, communicate effectively with members of an interdisciplinary team, and recognize the importance of treating every patient with dignity and respect.

Previously, I served as a Behavioral Health Specialist in the Emergency Department at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center, where I supported children and adolescents experiencing mental health crises. This experience gave me valuable insight into the challenges families face when seeking behavioral health services for their children. It also strengthened my understanding of the importance of timely access to care, clear communication, and collaboration among healthcare professionals. I recognize that connecting families with the appropriate level of treatment requires compassion, patience, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate sensitive information in a professional and supportive manner.

My Master’s degree in healthcare administration has further prepared me to contribute to the operational and coordination responsibilities of an admissions role. Through my education, I have developed a stronger understanding of healthcare systems, quality improvement, ethical decision-making, and the importance of efficient processes in supporting positive patient outcomes. I understand that an effective admissions process involves more than gathering information; it also requires helping families understand available services, coordinating next steps, maintaining accurate documentation, and communicating with appropriate team members to facilitate access to care.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it combines behavioral health, family engagement, and healthcare coordination. I would welcome the opportunity to help adolescents and their families navigate what can often be an overwhelming treatment-seeking process. I understand the importance of approaching these conversations without judgment, protecting confidential information, and helping families feel heard while ensuring their needs are communicated appropriately to the clinical team. I am also prepared to bring organization, accountability, and professionalism to a virtual work environment while maintaining a strong focus on responsiveness and service.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, educational background, and commitment to improving access to care could contribute to the admissions team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of helping adolescents and their families take meaningful steps toward treatment, recovery, and improved well-being.

Sincerely,
Stephenie Shelton

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy 

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With experience in behavioral health, admissions and intake coordination, therapeutic foster care, and crisis intervention, I believe my professional background and passion for helping others would make me a strong addition to your team.

Throughout my career, I have gained hands-on experience managing referrals, completing intake processes, coordinating placements, and communicating with families, providers, and community agencies. In my current roles as a Therapeutic Foster Care Case Manager and Overnight Emergency Placement Supervisor, I regularly assist individuals experiencing behavioral health challenges while ensuring they are connected with appropriate services and resources.

My experience working remotely has strengthened my ability to manage responsibilities independently, stay organized, maintain accurate documentation, and communicate effectively without constant supervision. I understand the importance of timely follow-up, confidentiality, and providing a positive experience from the initial point of contact through the coordination of services.

I also recognize that individuals and families seeking mental health or substance use treatment may be experiencing some of the most difficult moments of their lives. I pride myself on approaching every interaction with compassion, patience, and professionalism while helping individuals feel heard, supported, and informed about their next steps.

I hold a Bachelor's degree in Social Science with a minor in Psychology and a Master's degree in Criminal Justice. I am also currently pursuing my Master of Social Work degree at Troy University. My education and professional experience have provided me with a strong understanding of behavioral health needs, crisis intervention, and person-centered care.

I would appreciate the opportunity to bring my experience, strong work ethic, and commitment to helping others to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how I can contribute to the continued success of your programs.

Sincerely,
Monica Cockfield

candidates.cover_letter:
October 21, 2026

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinators
Dear Hiring Team,
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at AWA. Your mission to help not only the youth you serve, but the family as a whole is a strong match for the work I have done throughout my career.
For more than ten years, I have worked in roles where accuracy and confidentiality were not optional. As a Program Manager at Community Violence Solutions, I audited 100–200 client records every month in an Excel-based database, maintaining 100% accuracy and strict confidentiality. I managed high-volume documentation workflows against firm compliance deadlines, cross-checked data across multiple platforms, and produced reports for county, state, and federal funders. I also supervised a team of five to seven employees and trained them on data entry and documentation, so I know how to keep detail-oriented work consistent across a team. The work that I completed was all done with love and care for the family unit. We thrived in helping youth and families throughout their healing process. 
Earlier in my career, I managed active caseloads of 30 to 50+ clients at a time, completing intakes, case data entry, and monthly documentation for each one. I also provided customer and tech support in person and by chat as a part-time Customer Support Specialist at Sprint, handling setups, activations, and troubleshooting. Answering calls, working with limited supervision, and adjusting to changing priorities are things I do every day. I work comfortably in Word, Excel, Outlook, Google Workspace, Zoom, and Teams, and I have spent several years working fully remotely.
What I would bring to AWA most of all is a deep respect for the people behind the records. I have spent my career helping people in difficult moments, and I understand how important it is that sensitive information reaches only the right hands. I am eager to build on that foundation by learning HIPAA regulations and AWA,s procedures, and by developing into a dependable, high-quality member of your team. As a fully bilingual English and Spanish speaker, I also communicate clearly and professionally with a wide range of customers.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience can support your team, and I can be reached at 415-948-3875 or lray1214@gmail.com.

Sincerely,

Lucia Ray-Guillen

education.summary:
The Community Health Worker Certificate 2 year Program is a structured course of study designed to prepare students for work in community-oriented public health, health care, and social service fields.
Community Health Workers serve as a two-way bridge between communities and essential health and social resources. Community Health Workers provide a wide range of services including outreach, health education, client-centered counseling, and case management services. They play a vital role in promoting health justice and reducing health inequalities or unequal rates of illness, disability, and death between communities.

October 21, 2026

Dear Hiring Team,

I believe the person answering that first phone call can make all the difference in whether someone takes the next step toward getting help. That is what caught my attention about this opportunity. You're not simply looking for someone to answer calls and schedule appointments. You're looking for someone who can recognize the importance of that moment, connect with the person on the other end of the phone, and help them move forward. That is exactly the kind of work I enjoy doing.

I bring a combination of remote admissions experience, behavioral health support, and genuine compassion for people who are navigating difficult circumstances. During my time with Ultimate Medical Academy, I worked remotely in admissions, interviewing prospective students, managing a high volume of inquiries, maintaining CRM records, and following up with individuals throughout the enrollment process. I ranked number one in my division and achieved 380% of my enrollment target. Those results came from more than meeting performance expectations. I understood how to build relationships, listen to people's needs, address their concerns, and remain consistent in my follow-through.

What makes my background especially relevant is that I also understand the importance of emotional support. Through my work with Youth Villages and my experience in family support counseling, I've worked with individuals and families facing behavioral challenges, emotional difficulties, and circumstances that require patience, compassion, and sound judgment. I've learned that people do not always know how to communicate what they need, especially when they're overwhelmed. Sometimes you have to listen beyond the initial question to understand how you can actually help.

I recognize that behavioral health admissions are different from educational admissions. Families seeking mental health or substance use treatment may be frightened, exhausted, or uncertain about what happens next. I would approach those conversations with the same care I would want someone to show my own family, while ensuring that inquiries, documentation, referrals, and follow-ups are handled professionally and accurately.

I'm comfortable working independently in a remote environment, managing multiple conversations and responsibilities, maintaining confidential information, and following through until the next step is clear. I would welcome the opportunity to learn your admissions processes and become a dependable part of the team supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

I am confident in what I bring to this position, but what matters most to me is the opportunity to use my experience in a way that genuinely impacts someone's life. I would love the opportunity to speak with you about how I can contribute to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Inez D. Kearse

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. My name is Gabriela Lloyd-Perez, and I am thrilled at the opportunity to join your team and support your mission of promoting mental health and emotional well-being for adolescents.

What I find most appealing about this particular position is the opportunity to work closely with families who want to support their teens' mental health. I am deeply passionate about using my own experiences to help others, and I believe that this role would allow me to do just that.

Having worked for several years already with Vibrant Emotional Health in the Disaster Distress Helpline’s Online Peer Support Program (DDH OPSC), I worked specifically with parents and caregivers to provide resources to assist with their children and teens.  In addition, I trained crisis counselors on the 988 crisis line and for the LGBTQI youth chat and text line. During my time in this position, I was able to assess callers who reached out to the 988 line for suicidal ideation and imminent danger. I was able to provide resources and schedule follow-up calls. 

Furthermore, I am highly organized, detail-oriented, and have excellent time management skills. I understand the importance of meeting deadlines and ensuring that programs run smoothly. I am also proficient in Microsoft Office and have experience working with databases and managing program budgets. Gabriela Lloyd-Perez

Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center

Dear hiring Team,

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. My experience spans behavioral health admissions, adolescent and family counseling, and substance use treatment. I would bring a steady, reassuring voice to those seeking help understanding their options and taking the next step toward care.

At GenPsych, I handled evening and weekend admissions calls, screened prospective clients, assessed level-of-care needs, and coordinated clinical acceptance. My work with the Drug Abuse Treatment Association at Suncoast Community High School included adolescent assessments, individual and family counseling, and connections to community resources. At Beach House, Origins, and Banyan, I have supported adults facing substance use and mental health concerns. This experience helps me communicate respectfully with both a worried parent seeking help for a teenager and an adult considering treatment.

I am proficient in Kipu and electronic medical record applications, with experience using Sunwave and prior Salesforce CRM experience. I understand the importance of accurate documentation, confidentiality, and clear communication with clinical colleagues. Running my own home-care agency also required me to organize competing priorities, resolve concerns, and take responsibility for follow-through.

I am seeking a full-time remote admissions role where I can apply these skills directly with callers and families. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my admissions background and family-centered approach could support your team. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,

Karen M. Lazar, MSW

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. With over nine years of experience in behavioral health services, including more than six years with Metrocare, I have developed a strong foundation in client engagement, psychosocial rehabilitation, care coordination, and supporting individuals with diverse mental health needs. I am confident that my experience, communication skills, and commitment to helping individuals access appropriate care would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your team.

Throughout my career, I have worked with children, adolescents, and adults, providing skills training and psychosocial rehabilitation services to support emotional well-being, daily functioning, and progress toward individualized treatment goals. My experience has strengthened my ability to build rapport, communicate with individuals and families, recognize barriers to care, and connect clients with appropriate resources and services. I understand the importance of approaching individuals and families with empathy, professionalism, and sensitivity, particularly when they are navigating mental health challenges or seeking support during difficult circumstances.

I recognize that the admissions process is often a critical first step in a family’s treatment journey. I would bring a compassionate, organized, and client-centered approach to helping families navigate that process, gathering relevant information, coordinating communication, and supporting timely access to appropriate treatment services. My behavioral health background has also equipped me to communicate effectively with multidisciplinary teams, maintain professional documentation, manage competing priorities, and approach sensitive situations with discretion and respect.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to apply my clinical experience in a role focused on connecting adolescents and families with the support and treatment they need. I value collaboration, accountability, and clear communication, and I am committed to helping create a positive and supportive experience from the initial point of contact through the admissions process.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, client-centered approach, and dedication to improving access to care align with the needs of your organization. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your team.

Sincerely,
Sandra M. Scruggs

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. Throughout my career in case management, higher education, crisis response, and community outreach, I have dedicated myself to helping individuals and families navigate difficult circumstances and access the support they need. Your commitment to providing adolescents with a safe, compassionate, and supportive environment strongly resonates with both my professional experience and personal values.

As a Case Manager with the Care & Assistance Team at Texas A&M University–Corpus Christi, I supported students experiencing mental health concerns, housing instability, financial hardship, family difficulties, and other challenges affecting their well-being. I conducted needs assessments, developed individualized action plans, coordinated referrals, and collaborated with campus and community partners to connect students with appropriate services. This experience strengthened my ability to recognize when individuals need additional support, respond with empathy, and provide consistent follow-up while respecting confidentiality and professional boundaries.

My experience as a Pretrial Officer for Bexar County further developed my ability to manage complex caseloads, assess individual circumstances, maintain accurate documentation, and connect individuals with community resources. Previously, as a police dispatcher and 911 operator, I learned to remain calm under pressure, communicate clearly during emergencies, and respond to sensitive situations with sound judgment. These experiences prepared me to work effectively with individuals experiencing distress while maintaining professionalism and compassion.

My commitment to helping vulnerable populations also extends into my community involvement. Through Ferro Family Ministries, our family's nonprofit organization, I have collaborated with churches and community volunteers across Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas, and Mexico to support underserved youth and families. Our outreach efforts have included helping individuals access basic necessities, coordinating charitable assistance, and organizing fundraising initiatives for families facing significant hardships. These experiences reinforced my belief that meaningful support begins with listening, understanding individual needs, and treating every person with dignity and respect.

I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy's focus on supporting teenagers and their families through challenging periods in their lives. I understand the importance of building trust, communicating without judgment, and working collaboratively with professionals and families to promote stability and positive outcomes. While my background is not in clinical counseling, I bring extensive experience in client support, crisis communication, resource coordination, and compassionate service.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my skills and dedication to Adolescent Wellness Academy's mission. 
Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my experience can support your team and the adolescents and families you serve.

Sincerely,
Michael A. Ferro

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With my professional background in substance use treatment and behavioral health, combined with my experience using Kipu and providing services through telehealth, I believe I would bring a valuable combination of clinical knowledge, technical proficiency, and compassion to your admissions team.

Throughout my career as a substance use disorder therapist and behavioral health professional, I have worked extensively with individuals experiencing addiction, co-occurring mental health conditions, trauma, and other complex challenges. My experience spans residential treatment, Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHP), and Intensive Outpatient Programs (IOP). This familiarity with multiple levels of care allows me to explain treatment options confidently, recognize individual needs, and help prospective clients and their families navigate what can often be an overwhelming process.

I also have hands-on experience with Kipu electronic medical records, clinical documentation, treatment coordination, and telehealth services. I understand the importance of accurate recordkeeping, confidentiality, HIPAA compliance, and timely communication in ensuring continuity of care. My clinical background has also strengthened my ability to work independently, prioritize responsibilities, and collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams.

Perhaps my greatest strength is my ability to connect with people, particularly during vulnerable or emotionally difficult moments. I understand that individuals reaching out for treatment may be frightened, hesitant, or unsure where to begin. I believe the first interaction with a treatment provider should communicate compassion, reassurance, and hope while offering clear, practical guidance toward the next step.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to use my clinical experience in a different but equally meaningful capacity. I recognize that the admissions process is often the beginning of someone's recovery journey, and I would find tremendous purpose in helping individuals and families access the care they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, familiarity with Kipu, and commitment to compassionate, client-centered care could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,
Chloé

Hiring Team

Dear Hiring Team,
I am writing to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position for Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. Your job description talks about being the first voice someone hears on one of the hardest days of their lives, and that really stuck with me. While I don't have formal hospital admissions or boarding department experience, I have spent years working right on the front lines of care. I have worked in group homes with adults dealing with mental health and addiction, in daycares, and as an activities coordinator in senior care. I am also incredibly structured when it comes to the paperwork side of things. I know how critical it is to follow up consistently so that no one gets left behind, and I pride myself on staying organized so that every single detail is tracked properly.
I am fully prepared to handle this role in a remote environment. I am highly self-motivated, stick to a disciplined routine, and manage my daily tasks independently without needing someone to watch over my shoulder. I am used to working with data tracking systems and software platforms, and I take details and HIPAA compliance very seriously. Plus, my background in early childhood education gives me an intuitive understanding of the developmental struggles that the teenagers and families reaching out to AWA are facing.
I would love the opportunity to talk with you about how my real-world care experience, confident phone presence, and dedication to behavioral health can help support your admissions team. Thank you so much for your time and consideration.

Emilita

Hiring Manager

RE: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

When a family or individual reaches out during one of the most vulnerable moments of their life, the very first voice they hear can shape their entire path toward healing. As a dedicated mental health advocate with extensive experience managing high-stakes crisis situations, active listening, and complex multi-platform coordination, I am thrilled to submit my application for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) and Principles Recovery Center (PRC).

My professional background is centered on de-escalating high-stress situations, building immediate trust, and guiding individuals toward safe, actionable next steps. In my current work handling real-time safety alerts and through my formal training as a 988 Crisis Hotline volunteer counselor, I am deeply accustomed to meeting people in moments of distress with warmth, composure, and zero judgment. Whether explaining levels of care, walking a worried parent through the intake process, or addressing common hesitations surrounding PHP and IOP treatment, I focus on creating a safe, human connection while ensuring seamless operational execution.

Mental health advocacy is not just my career focus; it is my life’s work. To further deepen my clinical foundation and long-term impact in behavioral health, I am actively enrolling in a counseling degree program next year. This academic commitment, paired with my daily crisis training and hands-on remote experience, allows me to speak about behavioral health and substance use care with authority, clarity, and deep personal empathy.

In addition to my human-centered approach, I thrive in fast-paced, fully remote environments where self-management and technological agility are essential. I am highly proficient in managing high-volume candidate and client pipelines using CRM systems, double-checking documentation for strict compliance, and tracking follow-ups so that no caller falls through the cracks.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my blend of crisis intervention skills, remote workflow precision, and passion for adolescent and adult recovery can support AWA and PRC’s growth. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Warmly,

Lanrella Barber

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills align with this position.

Sincerely,
Ruth Kesseh

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. As a Certified Peer Recovery Specialist with national certification and hands-on experience in behavioral health admissions, intake coordination, insurance verification, and Kipu EMR, I bring a strong combination of operational knowledge, clinical understanding, and compassionate communication to this opportunity.

Throughout my career in behavioral health and substance use treatment, I have supported individuals and families during some of their most challenging and vulnerable moments. My professional experience includes managing intake inquiries, assisting with admissions processes, verifying insurance benefits, coordinating treatment referrals, maintaining accurate electronic health records, and helping individuals navigate appropriate levels of care. I am familiar with PHP and IOP treatment settings and understand the importance of timely communication, accurate documentation, and a seamless admissions experience.

My hands-on experience with Kipu EMR has strengthened my ability to manage patient information, maintain organized records, and support efficient clinical and administrative workflows. Additionally, my background providing remote behavioral health services has equipped me with the independence, adaptability, and attention to detail necessary to succeed in a fast-paced virtual admissions environment.

Beyond my technical qualifications, I bring a genuine passion for connecting individuals with life-changing treatment. Through my training in Motivational Interviewing, Wellness Recovery Action Planning (WRAP), Mental Health First Aid for Youth and Adults, trauma informed care, and overdose prevention, I have developed the ability to establish trust, navigate sensitive conversations, and support individuals experiencing mental health and substance use challenges.

I understand that for many adolescents and families, the admissions process represents their first step toward healing. I take pride in ensuring that every interaction is handled with professionalism, empathy, urgency, and respect. My goal is always to help individuals feel supported while making the process of accessing treatment as clear and manageable as possible.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it allows me to combine my admissions experience, technical proficiency, and commitment to behavioral health advocacy in a meaningful remote role. I am confident that my familiarity with Kipu, insurance verification, treatment coordination, and patient engagement would allow me to contribute positively to your admissions team from day one.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, qualifications, and dedication to helping individuals access quality behavioral health treatment align with the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

Jennifer Gribble
CPRS, NCPRSS

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With years of experience as a Physical Therapy Aide, along with front-desk, patient intake, scheduling, phone communication, and administrative experience, I have developed a strong foundation in patient care and a genuine passion for helping others feel supported, understood, and encouraged throughout their healthcare journey.

Throughout my healthcare experience, I have learned how important it is to make every patient feel welcome, respected, and comfortable. I consider myself a compassionate, positive, and motivating person with strong listening and communication skills. I enjoy building connections with people, understanding their concerns, and helping them feel more confident as they navigate their care. I also have experience handling phone calls, coordinating appointments, maintaining patient records, and managing administrative responsibilities. My remote work experience has further strengthened my ability to stay organized, manage responsibilities independently, and follow through consistently.

In addition, I speak four languages, which allows me to connect with people from diverse backgrounds and appreciate the importance of clear, compassionate communication. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming and vulnerable experience. I believe that a warm voice, a patient listener, and a supportive first interaction can make a meaningful difference for someone seeking help.

My passion for mental health is also personal. Having a close friend who struggled with mental health challenges helped me recognize how important it is for people to feel heard, supported, and treated without judgment. That experience deepened my desire to be part of an environment where individuals and families can find hope, guidance, and access to the care they need.         I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I believe my combination of behavioral health quality assurance, nursing home intake, insurance verification, and remote work experience makes me a strong candidate for this role. I bring both the administrative skills needed to help move the admissions process forward and an understanding of the importance of treating individuals and families with compassion when they are seeking care.

In my current role with Vibrant Emotional Health, I review 988 crisis calls, chats, and texts to evaluate interaction quality, adherence to established protocols, risk assessment, and appropriate crisis response. This experience has strengthened my ability to recognize concerns, pay attention to important details, assess whether established procedures are followed, and understand the importance of appropriate responses in sensitive situations. Working in crisis services has also reinforced that the way people are treated when they reach out for help matters. I would bring that same level of care, attentiveness, and professionalism to conversations with adolescents and families exploring treatment options.

My previous experience in a nursing home setting also provided me with hands-on experience in intake and insurance verification. I understand that an organized intake process requires accuracy, follow-through, and clear communication. I would use those skills to help families understand what to expect, identify the next steps in the admissions process, and move forward without unnecessary confusion.

I also bring experience working remotely, where independence, accountability, organization, and consistent communication are important. My quality assurance background has further developed my attention to detail and appreciation for accurate documentation and established procedures. I understand that admissions coordination involves more than answering inquiries; it requires keeping track of outstanding steps, following up appropriately, and helping ensure that people do not get lost in the process of seeking services.

As I pursue my Master of Social Work, I continue to strengthen my understanding of behavioral health, person-centered care, and the challenges individuals and families may face when trying to access support. I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it allows me to combine my administrative and behavioral health experience with my commitment to helping people connect with appropriate services. I would value the opportunity to help adolescents and their families navigate the admissions process with clarity, respect, and compassion while supporting the team’s efforts to maintain an organized and responsive admissions pipeline.

Thank you for considering my application. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in intake, insurance verification, remote work, and behavioral health quality assurance could benefit Adolescent Wellness Academy and the families it serves.

Best regards,
Nycole Alexandre

Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,
I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With four years of experience in an inpatient adolescent psychiatric setting, including direct experience with admissions paperwork and insurance-related processes, as well as my current experience as a Registered Behavior Technician, I bring a combination of administrative experience and a strong passion for supporting youth and families navigating mental health challenges.
At the beginning of my time in the inpatient psychiatric setting, I worked in intake, where I gained hands-on experience completing admissions paperwork and handling insurance-related processes. This experience gave me valuable insight into the administrative side of connecting individuals with care and the importance of helping families navigate these processes accurately and efficiently. Throughout my four years in the hospital, I also supported adolescents experiencing a wide range of challenges, including mental health crises, suicidal ideation, substance use concerns, and family conflict. These experiences strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy, remain calm in challenging situations, and treat every individual with patience and respect.
In my current role as a Registered Behavior Technician, I continue to develop my skills in behavioral support, communication, and individualized care. Working with young children has further strengthened my understanding of the importance of meeting individuals where they are and collaborating with others to support positive outcomes. Across both roles, I have learned the value of compassion, professionalism, attention to detail, and building trust with the individuals and families I serve.
I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it brings together my previous admissions experience and my continued commitment to adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. I would be proud to help adolescents and their families navigate the admissions process and take an important first step toward receiving the care they need.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, administrative experience, and dedication to supporting youth and families could contribute to the Adolescent Wellness Academy team.
Sincerely,
Brylie murcko

candidates.cover_letter:
Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment
October 20, 2026
Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center
Dear Hiring Team,
When a parent calls about a struggling teenager, or an adult finally reaches out about their substance use, the first voice they hear matters. I have spent more than 20 years being that voice, and I would love to bring that experience to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator.
My career has been built on admissions, assessment, and referral work. At National Healthcare Associates, I handled inbound referrals from several hospital systems at once for multiple facilities, screened each client against admission criteria, and decided whether to accept, deny, or refer them elsewhere. I verified benefits, secured Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial authorizations, and advocated directly with insurers to keep admissions from stalling. Before that, I spent 17 years as Regional Clinical Admissions Director for Kindred Healthcare, managing the full referral to admission cycle for adults with psychiatric and behavioral needs, including co-occurring drug and alcohol use disorders.
I am used to owning my pipeline without daily direction. At Kindred I independently ran a four-state territory, building relationships with case managers, social workers, and discharge planners both virtually and in person, and following up consistently until every referral had a clear outcome. That work generated enough admissions that the organization opened additional units and a new facility. I am comfortable working in CRM and EMR systems, including EPIC, Navi, and Allscripts, and I keep accurate, HIPAA-compliant records.
I also bring a counselor's foundation. I hold an M.S. in Mental Health Counseling and an M.S.Ed. in School Counseling from Syracuse University, my early clinical work included adolescents in day treatment and residential programs, and I served as board president of YouthHarbor. As a Reiki Master Teacher and owner of Beehive Wellness, I meet people in difficult moments with calm and compassion, which is exactly how I would greet your callers.
I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can help families and adults move from that first call to a clear next step. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Keli Scott

Dear Hiring Manager,

	I am writing to express my interest in your Virtual Admission Coordinator position through Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a strong background in research and clinical work, I am confident I can contribute effectively to your team through my administrative knowledge, interpersonal skills, compassion, knowledge of substance use and mental health, and data collection experience.

	My bachelor’s degree in psychology from Clemson University has given me the skills to apply statistical analysis and clinical administrative work in my current and past positions. As a Research Assistant at the Medical University of South Carolina, I conduct 20 interviews weekly and record all data through REDCap, Box, and Excel. In these interviews, I lead with empathy and understanding when discussing each patient's circumstances and communicate with their therapist accordingly. While administering assessments during appointments, I ensure that I am clear with the participant about what is expected during our discussions and give them resources when necessary. Each week, I update all logs and REDCap to reflect new data and create weekly meeting agendas to update my team on participant recruitment and enrollment. I have excelled in maintaining IRB materials by submitting all amendments and continuing reviews. My current position highlights skills that I thoroughly enjoy, such as working with participants and conducting assessments, which is why I would be thrilled to apply these to this role.

	My previous role as a Registered Behavior Technician enabled me to focus on child therapy. I implemented Applied Behavior Analysis with patients aged four to sixteen. It was essential to be thoroughly versed in each client's clinical assessments, protocols, and behavioral functioning. Data collection was the main focus of this position, so I excelled at meeting each goal and collecting all necessary data points during each session. My data collection was thorough and exceeded expectations, achieving at least 80 percent each time for my client’s learning objective.

In my previous research at Clemson University, I strengthened my interpersonal skills by recruiting deaf and hearing individuals for my research project, which allowed me to receive feedback and learn more about emotion and cognition. I also practiced several assessments with other students to learn the proper language and resources to provide based on each individual's circumstances. My experience throughout school and in my current or past positions has given me thorough experience communicating with individuals about personal topics and finding them the right resources that are applicable. I believe these experiences align with the requirements of your virtual admissions coordinator position, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute them to your team. Thank you for considering my application, and I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you in greater detail.
Sincerely,
Megan Pfizenmayer

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

When I read about your commitment to creating a place where troubled teens and their families feel safe, loved, cared for, and no longer alone, it truly touched my heart. I believe every child deserves to feel supported, understood, and accepted, especially during some of the most challenging years of their lives. Adolescence can already be difficult, and when mental health challenges or substance use become part of that journey, having a compassionate support system can make a tremendous difference. This is one of the reasons I am so passionate about the opportunity to join Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Helping people has always been something that brings me a genuine sense of purpose. During my time as a Case Manager with Prevention Central, I had the opportunity to work directly with individuals and families facing various challenges. I conducted assessments, developed individualized case plans, identified barriers, coordinated supportive services, and connected clients with community resources. What I enjoyed most was getting to know the individuals I served, listening to their concerns, understanding their circumstances, and working alongside them to find solutions. I learned that no two individuals are the same, and sometimes making a difference begins with simply taking the time to listen and showing someone that their situation matters.

I understand how important the first point of contact can be when a parent reaches out seeking help for their child. They may be frightened, overwhelmed, frustrated, or simply unsure of what to do next.  I believe the person answering that call has an opportunity to provide more than information. They can offer reassurance, compassion, and a sense of hope. I would never want a parent or teenager to feel like they are just another phone call or admission. I want them to feel heard, respected, and supported while helping them move toward the care they need.

In addition to my case management background, I worked remotely as an Intake Coordinator with All County Health Care, where I assisted clients through the intake process, gathered sensitive information, reviewed documentation, verified eligibility, coordinated services, and maintained confidential records. This experience strengthened my ability to work independently, manage multiple responsibilities, communicate professionally, and remain organized in a fast-paced environment. I understand that admissions require both compassion and urgency because individuals and families seeking treatment should not have to experience unnecessary delays in accessing care.

I am currently nearing completion of my Bachelor of Social Work, a goal that means a great deal to me because I know this is the field where my heart belongs. My training in Trauma-Informed Care, Motivational Interviewing, Mental Health First Aid, and suicide prevention has further strengthened my commitment to meeting people where they are and treating every individual with dignity and understanding. Although my direct admissions experience has not been specifically within a substance use treatment facility, I bring years of transferable experience in intake, case management, client advocacy, and working with vulnerable populations. I am confident in my ability to learn your admissions processes and contribute positively to your team.

What resonates with me most about your mission is the belief that healing happens through connection, compassion, and community.  Families need to know they are not alone in navigating these challenges. While an Admissions Coordinator may not provide the treatment itself, I believe we play an important role in helping families take that first step toward healing.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to interview. I am not simply looking for another job. I am looking for an opportunity to continue making a difference in the lives of individuals and families

Sincerely,
Stacy Scott

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Master of Science in Criminal Behavior, a bachelor’s degree in Psychology, and professional experience in healthcare administration, family services, and the legal field, I have developed strong communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills that I believe would translate well into this position. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to support adolescents, adults, and families as they navigate the process of seeking mental health and substance use treatment.

During my time at Bellbrook Family Practice, I gained extensive experience communicating with patients, coordinating appointments, managing medical records, and serving as a point of contact between patients, healthcare providers, and pharmacies. I regularly handled high volumes of phone calls, responded to patient inquiries, coordinated paperwork, and maintained sensitive medical information. This experience taught me the importance of patience, accuracy, confidentiality, and clear communication, particularly when assisting individuals who may be experiencing uncertainty or frustration.

Additionally, my internship with the Greene County Family Visitation Center allowed me to work directly with children and families navigating challenging circumstances. Through supervised visitation services, behavioral observations, and court-related documentation, I developed a greater understanding of the importance of providing compassionate, nonjudgmental support while maintaining professional boundaries. My current position with the Montgomery County Prosecutor’s Office has further strengthened my ability to manage confidential information, maintain detailed records, and balance multiple responsibilities in a fast-paced professional environment.

My graduate education has also provided me with a deeper understanding of psychological disorders, substance use, behavioral health assessment, and the social and environmental factors that influence mental health. I recognize that reaching out for treatment can be an overwhelming experience, particularly for adolescents and families who may be unfamiliar with the process. I would welcome the opportunity to help make that first interaction a positive one by providing clear information, reassurance, and consistent follow-through.

I am enthusiastic about the possibility of contributing to an organization dedicated to making behavioral healthcare more accessible. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my educational background, healthcare experience, and commitment to supporting individuals and families could contribute to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you.

Sincerely,
Madelyn Gilpin

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the **Virtual Admissions Coordinator: Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment** position. With my  experience supporting individuals with behavioral health needs and mental illness, I am confident that my clinical support skills, compassion, communication abilities, and dedication to patient care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my previous role at a 140-bed private psychiatric hospital, I provided care and support to adult patients ranging from geriatric individuals to returning veterans. Working under the direction of nursing and medical staff, I helped patients adjust to new routines, participate in social and therapeutic activities, and complete daily living tasks. I monitored patient behavior, maintained appropriate boundaries, assessed safety concerns, and responded effectively to crisis situations, including assisting with restraints when necessary to prevent injury.

In addition to my direct patient-care experience, I have developed strong skills in behavioral health referrals, admissions, and intake coordination. I am comfortable answering inbound calls and responding to inquiries from clients, parents and guardians, families, referral sources, and healthcare providers. I communicate with patience, empathy, and professionalism while gathering essential information, identifying immediate concerns, and helping families understand available treatment options.

I am familiar with explaining Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHP) and Intensive Outpatient Programs (IOP) in clear, caring, and easy-to-understand language. I understand that families seeking adolescent mental health or substance use treatment may be experiencing significant stress, and I approach each interaction with sensitivity, respect, and a nonjudgmental attitude. I can help families understand program expectations, levels of care, next steps, and the admissions process while ensuring that urgent safety concerns are communicated promptly to the appropriate clinical staff.

My additional qualifications include:

- Answering inbound calls and responding professionally to inquiries from adolescents, parents, guardians, families, providers, and referral sources  
- Gathering accurate demographic, clinical, insurance, and referral information during initial conversations  
- Screening prospective clients for program fit based on presenting concerns, treatment needs, age, safety considerations, and level of care  
- Explaining PHP, IOP, mental health, and substance use treatment services in a clear and compassionate manner  
- Recognizing potential safety concerns and escalating urgent situations according to established protocols  
- Verifying insurance eligibility and benefits and assisting with authorization-related information  
- Coordinating clinical assessments, intake appointments, admission dates, and required paperwork  
- Communicating with families, providers, clinicians, and other members of the treatment team to support a smooth admissions process  
- Following up consistently with every caller until the individual is scheduled, connected with services, or appropriately referred elsewhere  
- Maintaining accurate and timely documentation in CRM and electronic medical record systems  
- Entering referral and admissions information accurately while protecting confidential patient information  
- Completing documentation in accordance with HIPAA requirements and organizational policies  
- Tracking referrals, follow-up activity, scheduling status, and outcomes to ensure that no inquiry is overlooked  
- Remaining organized, responsive, and professional while managing multiple calls, referrals, and admissions tasks  
- Monitoring patient safety, behavior, vital signs, and overall condition in a psychiatric hospital setting  
- Supporting patients with personal care, daily activities, socialization, and rehabilitation  
- Remaining calm and effective during high-stress conversations and crisis situations  

I am passionate about helping adolescents and families connect with the appropriate behavioral health and substance use treatment services. My combination of hands-on psychiatric experience, referral coordination, insurance verification, admissions support, documentation, and strong interpersonal skills would allow me to contribute effectively to your virtual admissions team.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with the needs of your organization. I look forward to hearing from you.

Allison Bertolino
Port Saint Lucie, FL 34983

October 20, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescence Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining Adolescence Wellness Academy. With over three years of experience in behavioral health admissions, client assessments, insurance verification, treatment coordination, and patient intake, I have developed a strong understanding of the importance of compassionate, efficient, and individualized care. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, professionalism, and dedication to your team and contribute to helping adolescents and their families access the support and treatment they need.

In my current role as Lead Day Time Admissions Coordinator at Archstone Behavioral Health, I oversee the admissions process from the initial inquiry through enrollment. My responsibilities include verifying insurance benefits, conducting comprehensive assessments and screenings, identifying potential substance use disorders, and helping determine appropriate levels of care. I also coordinate travel arrangements, maintain accurate and confidential client records, and collaborate with probation officers and court officials when coordinating mandated treatment services. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, communicate effectively with individuals and families during difficult circumstances, and ensure a smooth and supportive admissions experience.

My previous experience as an Admissions Coordinator with Magnolia Ranch Recovery and Genesis Detox further developed my skills in client communication, treatment coordination, documentation, and collaboration with multidisciplinary teams to support individualized treatment planning. In addition, my experience as a Customer Service Manager strengthened my leadership, problem-solving, organization, and conflict-resolution skills. I understand the importance of building trust, responding to concerns with empathy, maintaining confidentiality, and helping people navigate what can often be an overwhelming process.

I believe my combination of behavioral health admissions experience, strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and compassionate approach would make me a valuable addition to Adolescence Wellness Academy. I am especially interested in the opportunity to apply my experience in a setting focused on supporting adolescents and their families, where clear communication, patience, and a commitment to quality care are essential.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and dedication to behavioral health can contribute to the mission of Adolescence Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely,
Allison Bertolino

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

Howdy! I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy because this role reflects the kind of work I have spent years doing: showing up for people when they are struggling, building trust when trust does not come easily, and helping individuals feel supported without judgment.
I bring more than seven years of direct behavioral health experience working with children, adolescents, adults, and older adults facing complex mental health, behavioral, and co-occurring substance use challenges. At Promises Behavioral Health, I supported adults ages 18 to 81 in residential and partial hospitalization settings. My work required constant observation, strong boundaries, de-escalation, crisis response, accurate documentation working with Kipu, teamwork with clinicians, and—perhaps most importantly—the ability to connect with people who were overwhelmed, guarded, resistant, or simply having a very difficult day.
Before that, at Halifax Behavioral Health, I worked with at-risk children and adolescents ages 4 to 17. That experience taught me how much can be communicated without words and how important consistency, patience, calmness, and genuine human connection are when someone does not yet feel safe enough to engage.
Those same lessons have followed me throughout nearly three decades of equine work. Through my current business, Healed By The Horse, I create individualized experiences centered on trust, emotional awareness, regulation, confidence, and connection. Horses have reinforced something I already knew from behavioral health: you cannot force trust. You earn it by being present, observant, consistent, and authentic.
That is what draws me to remote work with Adolescent Wellness Academy.
I understand that meaningful mental health is not achieved by treating a diagnosis while overlooking the person living with it. People need to know that someone sees them, hears them, respects their experience, and will continue showing up. I would bring that mindset—along with substantial hands-on behavioral health experience, strong observational skills, compassion, professional boundaries, and a steady presence—to the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role.
I am also comfortable working independently, communicating virtually, documenting electronically via Kipu, learning new systems, and collaborating closely with multidisciplinary care teams. The opportunity to provide meaningful support within a virtual treatment environment is especially appealing to me.
I would be proud to bring my experience, patience, intuition, and very genuine commitment to helping people to Adolescent Wellness Academy. 

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you about how I could contribute to your team and, most importantly, to the individuals you serve.

Warmly,

Kris Secor
