candidates.cover_letter:
Hello,
In my career, I have grown from a behavior therapist, classroom teacher, and
now program coordinator. Over time, I have built up a toolkit of skills that
range from teaching, organization, public speaking, and program
coordination. I spent 9 years as a classroom teacher at a Title 1 school and
currently serve as the Patient Academics Services Coordinator for Johns
Hopkins All Children’s Hospital. I have a combined 13 years of education
experience, the most recent 3 years being in a leadership position. I have
worked in a variety of settings with diverse populations of different needs.
I have had the great pleasure to rebuild the Patient Academics Services (PAS)
program from the ground up. We now serve both the community and the
Johns Hopkins All Children’s community as a whole. Within the PAS I have
built my skills in budgeting, public speaking, program planning, and
networking. Additionally, I have had the great fortune to build the PAS team
from one to four, and help set up both the hospital school teachers and
teacher’s aide for success by on-boarding, training, and creating regular
huddles to discuss successes, needs, and challenges that we regularly face.
Working in a hospital setting has built my knowledge and skills in working
with children and young adults with disabilities. In this setting I see patients
who have cognitive, behavioral, medical, and psychological needs. I have
learned a great deal in liaisoning between the hospital and school districts
about advocating for patient needs and finding the best educational plan
that fits their current situations. I have worked with patients who have cystic
fibrosis, eating disorders, traumatic brain injury, and many other
chronic/acute diseases. Much of my role is spent educating school staff
about the needs these patients will have upon school re-entry. I have had run
education settings within the hospital on communication with patients from
a teacher perspective as well. Not only have I worked as an advocate for
these patients, I have also been their teacher. I regularly work with patients
as a bedside teacher, jumping in and teaching everything from 1st grade
English to 12th grade AP Physics.
I believe that if I were to be given this opportunity, I would be able to make
the program flourish. I would work hard to identify the needs of the
community. I truly submit to the concept of a growth mindset and I believe I
will be an asset to your team.
Sincerely,
Raye Steinman

candidates.cover_letter:
To whom it may concern,

I am excited to apply for the Adolescent Services Manager position. My background in
education and student services has given me extensive experience leading teams,
coordinating day-to-day operations, managing competing priorities, and creating
structured environments where young people can feel supported and successful. I am
especially drawn to this role because it combines the organization and problem-solving I
enjoy with the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the experience of
adolescents and their families.

Throughout my career, I have been responsible for coordinating programs, supporting
staff and students, managing schedules and logistics, maintaining accurate records, and
making sure day-to-day operations stay on track. In my previous roles, I have worked
with multidisciplinary teams, coordinated services and resources, addressed concerns
as they arose, and communicated with a wide range of stakeholders. I am comfortable
stepping in when something isn't working, figuring out what needs to be done, and
creating a practical solution.

I also understand the importance of consistency when working with adolescents. Clear
expectations, reliable routines, strong communication, and a supportive environment can
make a significant difference. I would bring a calm, organized approach to supervising
Wellness Coordinators, providing clear direction and accountability while also being
available to support the team when challenges arise.

My experience has also required me to balance many details at once, including
schedules, documentation, compliance requirements, events, resources, and
unexpected issues. I am someone who naturally looks ahead, notices what needs
attention, and takes pride in keeping things organized. I believe those strengths would
translate well to managing program flow, staff coverage, attendance, intake coordination,
safety procedures, and the administrative responsibilities of this position.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, organization, and problem-
solving skills to Adolescent Wellness Academy and contribute to a program where
adolescents and families feel safe, respected, and supported.

Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you
about how my background could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,

Melanie Negron
